headline_marked: [[PM Tarique Rahman departs for New York]] to attend 81st UN General Assembly
headline: PM Tarique Rahman departs for New York to attend 81st UN General Assembly
summary: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman is leading a 26-member delegation to the 81st UNGA, where he will address the assembly on September 24 and engage in various high-level discussions and bilateral meetings.
details: Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, accompanied by his wife Dr Zubaida Rahman and other entourage members, departed Dhaka for New York early today to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA). Their Turkish Airlines flight took off from Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport at 6:05am.

The Prime Minister is scheduled to address the UNGA on September 24, leading a 26-member delegation. LGRD and Cooperatives Minister Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan, BNP Acting Secretary General Advocate Ruhul Kabir Rizvi, and other senior officials were present at the airport to see him off.

The flight is scheduled to reach Istanbul Airport at 11:35am Turkey time after an eight-hour-45-minute journey. Following a two-hour-35-minute stopover, it will depart Istanbul at 2:10pm and arrive at John F Kennedy International Airport in New York at 5:55pm local time.

Upon arrival, Bangladesh’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Irene Zubaida Khan, and Ambassador to the US, Tareq Md Ariful Islam, will receive the Prime Minister. He will then be taken to the Hyatt Grand Central New York for his stay.

PM Rahman's UNGA engagements begin on September 22 with a welcome breakfast hosted by UN Secretary-General António Guterres. He will also join world leaders at the session's opening and attend a reception hosted by the US president.

On September 23, Tarique Rahman will engage with international charitable and humanitarian organizations at a breakfast meeting. He will then address a meeting on tackling the global inequality crisis, jointly organized by Brazil, South Africa, Norway, and Spain.

He is also scheduled to attend a high-level meeting on "Climate Action and the Just Transition," convened at the initiative of the UN secretary-general. Later that day, at a Bangladesh-hosted side event on the Rohingya crisis, he will seek greater international cooperation for the earliest possible repatriation of forcibly displaced Rohingyas to Myanmar.

During climate-related meetings, the Prime Minister is expected to highlight Bangladesh’s position as a climate-vulnerable country. He will emphasize climate finance, adaptation, technology transfer, loss and damage, and climate justice.

On September 24, Tarique Rahman will deliver opening remarks at a high-level meeting on the existential threats posed by sea-level rise. He will also be the chief guest at a Bangladesh-hosted side event on maternal and newborn health and midwifery, highlighting government initiatives and future plans.

On the sidelines of the UNGA, the Prime Minister is scheduled to hold bilateral meetings with the Crown Prince of Kuwait and the prime ministers of Croatia, Bhutan, Thailand, Pakistan, and Haiti. These talks are expected to cover political and economic relations, trade, investment, development cooperation, and the Rohingya crisis.

He is also scheduled to meet UN Secretary-General António Guterres, the president of the European Council, and the president of the World Bank Group. Meetings are also planned with the UN secretary-general’s special envoy on Myanmar, and the UN high commissioners for refugees and human rights.
The Prime Minister is scheduled to depart New York for Dhaka from JFK International Airport at 11:00pm local time on September 25 via Emirates flight EK202.

headline_marked: [[New pay scale raises minimum basic to Tk 20,000]] and maximum to Tk 1,56,000
headline: New pay scale raises minimum basic to Tk 20,000 and maximum to Tk 1,56,000
summary: The new pay scale, effective retrospectively from July 1, 2026, will be rolled out in phases, impacting 24 lakh civil and defence employees and 9.25 lakh pensioners across Bangladesh.
details: The new pay scale's basic salary implementation will cost the government Tk 37,372 crore in two phases. This covers civil, defence, and judicial personnel, along with pensioners.

Of this sum, Tk 23,311 crore is for civil and defence services, while Tk 14,061 crore is allocated for pensioners, gratuity, and lump grants. The exact funds for this fiscal year will be determined once pay across grades is fixed.

The new pay scale will take effect retrospectively from July 1, 2026, and will be rolled out gradually over four phases. Full implementation of restructured salaries and allowances is estimated to add Tk 1,05,580 crore to the government's annual expenditure.

Currently, Bangladesh's public sector workforce includes 24 lakh civil and defence services employees and 9.25 lakh pensioners. Tk 44,000 crore has already been earmarked in this fiscal year's budget for the ninth pay scale.

Under the revised structure, the minimum basic pay will rise from Tk 8,250 to Tk 20,000, and the maximum fixed basic salary will increase from Tk 78,000 to Tk 1,56,000. Special grades for top officials will see cabinet and principal secretaries draw Tk 1,72,000 basic.

With allowances, the total monthly payout for cabinet and principal secretaries will be Tk 2,47,600, alongside vehicle privileges. Grade 1 officials will earn a basic salary of Tk 1,56,000, bringing their gross monthly earnings to approximately Tk 2.25 lakh.

Fresh recruits in Grade 9 via BCS will start with a gross monthly salary of Tk 66,800, up from Tk 36,800. Grade 20 employees in Dhaka will see their total monthly pay rise to Tk 35,500, an increase from Tk 15,112.
Employees in Grades 10 to 20 will receive a 50 percent basic salary increase in the first phase, effective July 1. Further increases of 25 percent will follow in January and July 2027.

Officials in Grades 1 to 9 will see a 40 percent basic salary rise in the first phase, with subsequent 30 percent increases in January and July 2027. The final phase, beginning January 1, 2028, will revise all other allowances across all 20 grades.
